title: Oncall Handoff Notes - Maya Singh (2026-03-04)
content:
Summary:
- Night shift (10pm-6am PST) summary and handoff notes. Primarily quiet, one transient degradation on hosted API (region us-west-2) around 02:15 PST. Follow-ups and temporary runbook edits below.

Incidents this shift:
1) Incident INC-9134 — 02:15-02:32 PST — Hosted API elevated 5xx rate (region: us-west-2)
   - Symptom: sudden spike in 502/504 from frontend LB to inference pool for a single customer route (/v1/generate).
   - Immediate mitigation: scaled up dedicated hot-pool for hosted API by +2 instances (manual scale via console) at 02:18. 5xx rate dropped to baseline by 02:25.
   - Root cause (prelim): autoscaler failed to trigger due to mis-evaluated CPU metric window; metric stream had a transient spike filtered by anomaly filter rule. Potentially related to metrics agent version 1.12.
   - Actions taken: created JIRA OPS-4821 to track autoscaler behavior and metric anomaly thresholds. Notified infra team in #infra-alerts.
   - TODO: add a temporary fallback policy to route to us-east-1 for affected customer route if us-west-2 shows >2x 5xx for 5m. (See temp procedure below.)

Operational notes / things to watch:
- Metrics agent on serving nodes currently at v1.12 (rolling upgrade in progress). If you see metric gaps or CPU anomalies, check agent logs: /var/log/metrics-agent/agent.log.
- Prefix caching alerts: saw 1 warning about stale cache keys around 01:40 but it self-healed. Keep an eye for repeated occurrences.
- Disk pressure: node s-pool-07 reported short-lived disk pressure (kube evictions) at 00:50; cleared after kubelet restarted. I've filed a follow-up ticket to increase ephemeral storage for that pool (OPS-4830).

Temporary runbook procedures (for this week) - put these in a visible place until autoscaler fix is deployed:
- If hosted API 5xx rate in a region > 2% for 3 consecutive 1-min windows AND traffic QPS > 500, do the following:
  1) Manually scale ring 'hosted-hotpool-<region>' +2 instances via Console -> Dedicated Pools -> Scale.
  2) If +2 doesn't reduce 5xx within 5m, trigger failover to fallback region (us-east-1): update routing rule for customer route to include fallback ring with weight 50% (Console: Routing -> Policies -> Edit).
  3) Notify customer-success and the affected customer via template: "We’re seeing elevated errors in us-west-2; routing some traffic to healthy region while we investigate."
- Quick commands (kubectl / internal CLI):
  - Check pod logs for autoscaler: kubectl -n infra logs deploy/autoscaler --since=30m
  - Force scale serving pool: internalctl serving scale --pool hosted-hotpool-us-west-2 --delta 2
  - Check LB health: curl -I https://health-load.us-west-2.redwood.ai/healthz

Notes about ongoing work and context:
- Autoscaler change in PR #342 (see linked GH) is slated for deploy later this week — it adjusts anomaly filter thresholds. Until deployed, prefer manual scaling when you see sustained 5xx spikes.
- We are tracking a possible correlation between metrics agent 1.12 and missed scale events. If you find consistent metric gaps, collect agent logs and attach to OPS-4821.

Open items / follow-ups (assigned):
- OPS-4821 (Maya) — root cause investigation for autoscaler behavior. Add logs, timeline, and propose threshold change.
- OPS-4830 (Jordan) — increase ephemeral storage for s-pool-07 and review scheduling constraints.
- Customer follow-up: Emily to send post-incident note to affected customer (cc: CS manager).

Draft runbook edits (things to incorporate formally):
- Add a short-circuit for routing if region 5xx > 2% for 5m and rolling deploys didn't start.
- Add a checklist to verify metrics-agent version and check /api/metrics/stream for gaps before concluding autoscaler misfire.
- Add clear escalation: if manual scale + routing failover needed twice in 24h for same customer, escalate to Eng Lead and SRE manager and open an incident review.

Quick reference links and snippets:
- Incident playbook (current): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRE/pages/123456789/Oncall+Runbook
- Autoscaler logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/query?query=autoscaler%20error&range=2h
- Internal CLI docs: internal.redwood.ai/ctl#serving

Personal notes / scratchpad (things I left half-done):
- Started a small doc draft to add fallback weighting templates in console; not finished (TODO: add exact route id and customer id).
- Need to validate the health-check thresholds for the LB; I changed them briefly during incident to be more forgiving. Revert plan: set back to 5s interval, 3 failures — but confirm with infra team before reverting.

If you take this shift:
- Check INC-9134 and OPS-4821 status first. If there are follow-ups, escalate to Jordan if it looks like persistent scaling misses.
- If anything spikes in us-west-2, prefer manual scale first (fastest) and then routing change if no improvement in 5m.
- Ping me (Maya) on Slack if you need context; I’ll be online until ~09:30 PST.

Unresolved questions (put these in OPS-4821):
- Why did anomaly filter ignore the CPU spike for that window? Need metric dump around 02:10-02:20.
- Is there a relationship between agent v1.12 and metric export cadence?

End.
plain_text_preview: Oncall night shift notes: one transient hosted-api 5xx event at 02:15 PST. Manual scale +2 resolved; created OPS-4821 to investigate autoscaler/metrics. Temporary runbook steps added. See linked artifacts.
